prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

This manifesto sets out proposals across immigration, public spending, taxation, public services, energy, policing, justice, education, welfare, Brexit, defence, housing, families, infrastructure, agriculture, fisheries, pensions/social care, constitutional change, and governance, with associated costings and savings.

Core pledges:
- Freeze non‑essential immigration; detain and remove illegal arrivals; new immigration department; offshore processing; restrict student dependants; 5‑year residency for benefits; higher employer NI (20%) for foreign workers with exemptions.
- Zero NHS waiting lists by using independent capacity, tax incentives for staff, vouchers when waiting times exceed set limits, and efficiency reforms.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; scrap energy levies and VAT on energy; expand domestic oil and gas.
- Reduce government waste via departmental efficiency (5%), ending interest on QE reserves, halving foreign aid, improving tax collection, and deregulation.

Tax and economy:
- Personal: Lift income tax start point to £20k; higher rate from £70k; cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap energy levies and VAT on bills; cut stamp duty (0% under £750k, 2% to £1.5m, 4% above); restore VAT‑free tourist shopping; reform inheritance tax (no IHT under £2m; 20% above with charity option).
- Business: Raise corporation tax threshold to £100k profits; cut main rate to 20% then 15% (year 3); abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k; later abolish business rates for high‑street SMEs, offset by a 4% online delivery tax; simplify planning; reduce employment regulation; simplify the tax code.

NHS and social care:
- Zero basic rate tax for frontline NHS and social care staff for 3 years; end training caps; write off student fees pro‑rata over 10 years of NHS service; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance; weekend theatres; better procurement; “Pharmacy First” approach; public inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms.
- Royal Commission on social care; close tax loopholes for offshore care‑home structures.

Energy and environment:
- Scrap Net Zero targets and related subsidies; fast‑track North Sea and shale; develop SMRs and other technologies.

Law, order, and justice:
- Recruit 40,000 police; increase stop and search; tougher sentences (including mandatory life for violent repeat offenders); expand prison capacity by 10,000 places; increase criminal justice budget to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; revise hate‑crime definitions; streamline policing, reduce paperwork.

Education:
- Curriculum review; restrict gender identity policies in schools; ensure single‑sex facilities and parental notification; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans and extend repayment; enforce entry standards; expand pupil referral units; promote 2‑year degrees.

Welfare and work:
- Incentivise work via higher tax threshold; target up to 2 million back to work; two‑strike rule on job offers; face‑to‑face assessments with exemptions for severe conditions.

Brexit and sovereignty:
- Scrap retained EU laws; abandon the Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate the Trade and Cooperation Agreement.

Defence and veterans:
- Raise defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by year 3 and 3% by year 6; pay review; legal protections; dedicated veterans department; recruit 30,000 for the army; reform procurement.

Housing:
- Fast‑track brownfield development; prioritise locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest deductibility for landlords; strengthen leaseholder protections.

Infrastructure and transport:
- Cancel remaining HS2; repeal ULEZ/low‑traffic schemes; no bans on petrol/diesel; accelerate regional road/rail upgrades; new utility ownership model (50% public/50% UK pension funds); cap standing charges.

Agriculture and fisheries:
- Increase farm budget to £3bn; replace climate‑linked subsidies; tackle supermarket power; “Buy British” targets; cut red tape; restrict foreign fishing access; expand patrols; rebuild processing.

Constitution and governance:
- Leave the ECHR; reform the House of Lords and civil service leadership; restrict postal voting; consider PR via referendum; British Bill of Rights; overhaul equalities and free‑speech laws; reform the BBC funding model; new anti‑corruption unit; oppose WHO pandemic treaty and a CBDC; retain cash.

Funding summary (annualised):
- Claimed savings: ~£150bn plus £10bn from growth assumptions.
- Claimed costs: ~£141bn.

TEXT_D:
Summary of key proposals (non-exhaustive)

Economy and tax
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish the main rate of self-employed NI during the next Parliament.
- Maintain rates of income tax and VAT; introduce a “Triple Lock Plus” so the State Pension and pensioner tax-free allowance rise by the highest of earnings, inflation, or 2.5%.
- 30 hours free childcare from 9 months to school start by Sept 2025; move Child Benefit to a household test starting taper at £120,000.
- Business: retain full expensing (explore extension to leasing), no rise in corporation tax, 10-point SME plan (business rates relief focus, prompt payments, Open Finance, regional mutual banks, keep key investment incentives).
- Regulation/Whitehall: reduce civil service to pre-pandemic size; halve spend on consultants; relocate roles out of London; expand digital/AI capability; Minimum Service Levels on strikes.

Infrastructure, innovation and trade
- Reallocate £36bn from HS2 Phase 2 to regional transport (roads, rail, bus), including Northern Powerhouse Rail (Manchester–Liverpool) and Midlands Rail Hub; electrify North Wales Main Line.
- Nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G in all populated areas; legal framework for automated vehicles; aviation SAF support; maritime connectivity review.
- R&D to £22bn/year; invest in compute for AI; advanced manufacturing plan; maintain R&D tax reliefs; support financial services competitiveness.
- Trade: implement CPTPP; pursue FTAs with India and GCC; deepen EU TCA without ceding sovereignty; maintain standards in NHS and food.

Education, skills and youth
- Ban mobile phones in school day; give parents access to curriculum materials; protect per-pupil funding in real terms.
- Advanced British Standard for 16–19 (broader study, English and maths to 18).
- 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by closing poor-outcome degree courses.
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (paid competitive military year or part-time civic service).

Welfare and work
- Tighten work capability assessments; overhaul fit notes via specialist teams; reform PIP with greater focus on needs and treatment access; stronger sanctions for long-term non-compliance; fraud bill to bolster DWP powers.

Health and social care
- NHS spending to rise above inflation annually; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First, modernise GP premises, add 50 Community Diagnostic Centres.
- £3.4bn tech upgrade: NHS App as single front door, AI diagnostics, data platforms; reduce managers by 5,500.
- Dental recovery plan (more NHS appointments, contract reform, rural “golden hellos”, vans); require new dentists to serve in NHS for a period or repay training.
- Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; women’s health actions (maternity safety, pelvic health, hubs); implement Cass Review; single-sex accommodation rights; expand youth/adult mental health access.

Borders, security and defence
- Legal annual cap on work/family migration that falls each year; raise salary thresholds; health checks and higher charges; restrict dependants; increase visa fees; expand returns deals.
- Monthly removals to Rwanda; seek international asylum reform; intensify organised immigration crime action.
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; at least £10bn for munitions; Defence Innovation Agency with 5% of budget for R&D plus 2% for exploitation; sustained support to Ukraine; Veterans’ Bill and benefits.

Policing, justice, and civic order
- 8,000 additional neighbourhood police; hotspot policing nationwide; facial recognition and anti-knife powers; Martyn’s Law.
- Tougher sentences for serious offenders; four new prisons; more foreign offender removals; expand fraud measures.
- New protest controls (e.g., face coverings bans, cumulative impact); protect schools from targeted protests; counter-extremism measures.

Energy, climate and environment
- Annual North Sea oil/gas licensing; new gas plants; treble offshore wind; two CCS clusters now and more later; expedite small modular reactors and approve Wylfa; expand interconnectors.
- Keep energy price cap; review standing charges; energy-efficiency vouchers and £6bn for home upgrades; onshore wind with local consent; solar away from best farmland; no fracking.
- Environment: deliver biodiversity targets, expand Blue Belt, moratorium on deep-sea mining, strengthen water regulation and penalties, river restoration fund, tree planting and urban greening, tougher fly-tipping penalties, deposit return scheme, limit new incinerators.

Housing and communities
- 1.6m homes in England; lift nutrient neutrality barriers with mitigation fees; fast-track brownfield; densify inner London; protect Green Belt.
- Permanent SDLT relief for first-time buyers up to £425k; new Help to Buy; CGT relief for landlords selling to sitting tenants; complete leasehold reform; renters’ reform with Section 21 abolition alongside court changes.
- £20m endowments for 105 towns; extend Shared Prosperity Fund; more Freeports and zones; Backing Drivers Bill (ban road pricing, reverse London ULEZ expansion, local referendums for 20mph/LTNs); extend £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament.

Food, rural and coastal
- Increase UK-wide farming budget by £1bn over the Parliament with inflation protection; legal food security target; 50% public food spend local/higher-standard; fast-track farm infrastructure; seasonal worker scheme with taper; £100m Seafood Fund successor; expand inshore opportunities; major flood defence investment.

Union and devolution
- Protect internal market and unfettered trade; extend UK-wide funds and investment zones; specific transport, energy, and industry projects across Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland; support for Windsor Framework implementation and legacy bodies.
